nodes.description: INT8 Attention Engine, DG32 Attention Engine Architecture. (from dr/source/dg32-architecture/dg32-2dom/story-architect-pack.md)

nodes.name: Clock Domain Crossing Bridges
nodes.description: Clock Domain Crossing Bridges, DG32 Attention Engine Architecture. Uses a 4-phase request-acknowledge handshake and 2-flop synchronisers instead of FIFOs because data crossings between domains occur rarely (batch loading and result write-back). (from dr/source/dg32-architecture/dg32-2dom/story-architect-pack.md)

nodes.name: DG32-2DOM Chip

nodes.name: Key/Value SRAM Buffers
nodes.description: Key/Value SRAM Buffers, DG32 Attention Engine Architecture. Loading keys and values once per kick and re-reading for each query row keeps bus occupancy at ~1%, avoiding severe bus contention with the control domain. (from dr/public/downloads/dg32-2dom-architecture-guide.md)

nodes.name: Bus and System Controller
nodes.description: Bus and System Controller, DG32 Attention Engine Architecture. With no on-die debugger halt, unmapped addresses must return bus errors rather than hanging the bus to prevent bricking the device. (from dr/public/downloads/dg32-lite-architecture-guide.md)

nodes.name: Key/Value Buffers
nodes.description: Key/Value Buffers, DG32 Attention Engine Architecture. Loading keys and values once and re-reading them keeps per-head bus traffic around 1% occupancy, preventing the engine from fighting the rest of the die for memory. (from dr/source/dg32-architecture/dg32-2dom-architecture.md)

nodes.name: dgrid_dshot
nodes.description: dgrid_dshot, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Extend slot 0xC in place rather than creating a new slot because the address map has no free slot without touching frozen decoder logic, RX/TX are mutually exclusive on same pads so one owner is safer, and timing registers can be shared. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dshot-rx-block-spec.pdf)

nodes.name: dgrid_dshot_tel
nodes.description: dgrid_dshot_tel, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Firmware supplies only exponent and mantissa {e, m}; hardware performs CRC, GCR, and transition encoding to limit firmware overhead to one register write per commutation update. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dshot-rx-block-spec.pdf)

nodes.name: dgrid_irq
nodes.description: dgrid_irq, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Allocates previously unused bit 7 in raw interrupt vector with dshot_rx_i defaulted to 1'b0 to avoid disturbing the frozen lite netlist. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dshot-rx-block-spec.pdf)

nodes.name: dgrid_lockstep_check
nodes.description: dgrid_lockstep_check, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dshot-rx-block-spec.pdf)

nodes.name: openframe_project_wrapper
nodes.description: openframe_project_wrapper, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Reuses existing PC_BIDIR pad class rather than introducing a new runtime-switched gpio_dm mode, relying on external pull-ups on the board. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dshot-rx-block-spec.pdf)

nodes.name: DGridRiscV Core (rv32imc Lockstep)
nodes.description: DGridRiscV Core (rv32imc Lockstep), DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. CPU has a hardwired PMA whitelist requiring addr[31] set or 0x1xxx_xxxx, which is why SRAM is at 0x9 and peripherals are at 0xC/0xD. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-datasheets-qfn64.pdf)

nodes.name: DMA Controller
nodes.description: DMA Controller, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. The top arbitrates LSU-priority over DMA. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-datasheets-qfn64.pdf)

nodes.name: CPU PMA Whitelist
nodes.description: CPU PMA Whitelist, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. A load or store is legal only if addr[31] is set or the address is in 0x1xxx_xxxx; that is why SRAM is mapped at 0x9000_0000 and peripherals at 0xC/0xD/0xE. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-datasheets-qfn64.pdf)

nodes.name: 3-Phase PWM Peripheral
nodes.description: 3-Phase PWM Peripheral, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-datasheets-qfn64.pdf)

nodes.name: 3-Phase PWM Controller
nodes.description: 3-Phase PWM Controller, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-datasheets-qfn64.pdf)

nodes.name: 64-pin QFN Package (SkyWater sky130A)
nodes.description: 64-pin QFN Package (SkyWater sky130A), DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Pinout shared between DG32-LITE and DG32-2DOM because attention engine is memory-mapped internally and adds no user pads. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-datasheets-qfn64.pdf)

nodes.name: QSPI-XIP Read Window

nodes.description: 32 KB Main SRAM, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-datasheets-qfn64.pdf)

nodes.description: Supervisor & Windowed Watchdog, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-datasheets-qfn64.pdf)

nodes.name: INT8 Attention Accelerator
nodes.description: INT8 Attention Accelerator, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Computes band of query rows of one head end to end (QK^T, softmax/EXP, E.V, requantise to int8) with shared LANES-wide MAC array, 256-entry u15 EXP table, and 40-bit numerator on clk_fast_i (114 MHz). (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: 64 KB Boot ROM
nodes.description: 64 KB Boot ROM, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Standalone boot without management core: emits banner on UART0, reads QSPI NOR flash header, copies image to SRAM via quad-output fast-read, jumps to SRAM. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: CORDIC Coprocessor
nodes.description: CORDIC Coprocessor, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Q1.31 rotation and vectoring coprocessor (N=20 iterations, 53-58 cycles) at 0xDE00_0000; magnitude is uncompensated by design. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: Dual RV32IMC Lockstep Core
nodes.description: Dual RV32IMC Lockstep Core, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Dual lockstep core running at 50 MHz design target on sky130A process with hardwired PMA whitelist. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: DShot ESC Engine
nodes.description: DShot ESC Engine, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. ESC engine at 0xC000_0000 pin-muxed onto PWM pads with 4 throttle channels sharing one bit-time counter. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: Fault CSR
nodes.description: Fault CSR, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Lockstep fault status and injection module at 0xD600_0000; sticky-first recording of mismatch causes. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: IRQ Aggregator
nodes.description: IRQ Aggregator, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Aggregates 16 interrupt sources (including timers, PWM trigger, ADC done, DMA, fault, SW, and ATTN) at 0xDF00_0000. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: 3-Phase PWM
nodes.description: 3-Phase PWM, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. 3-phase center-aligned PWM with programmable deadtime, center-aligned ADC trigger, and async hardware brake at 0xD800_0000. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: SAR ADC
nodes.description: SAR ADC, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. 8-bit differential SAR analog macro operating at 1.8 V user supply (vccd1) at 0xDB00_0000. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: 32 KB SRAM
nodes.description: 32 KB SRAM, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Main data and code execution memory at 0x9000_0000, required because CPU fetch bus is ROM-only and cannot execute directly from QSPI-XIP. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: Supervisor / wWDT
nodes.description: Supervisor / wWDT, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Windowed watchdog and rail monitor at 0xD700_0000; faults if kicked before WDTMIN or after WDTMAX. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: Fault CSR Block
nodes.description: Fault CSR Block, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Maintains sticky fault status and lockstep-compare mismatch events (base 0xD600_0000) (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-lite-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: PWM Half-Bridge Subsystem
nodes.description: PWM Half-Bridge Subsystem, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Complementary outputs with programmable dead-time and hardware brake forcing all low to respect driver shoot-through specs (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-lite-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: QSPI-XIP Controller
nodes.description: QSPI-XIP Controller, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Base 0x1000_0000; data read window for loads, not instruction fetch (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-lite-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: SAR ADC Peripheral
nodes.description: SAR ADC Peripheral, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. 8-bit differential SAR ADC macro; trim/comp taps left unrouted because routing them made the die unroutable, so runs untrimmed (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-lite-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: SAR ADC Differential Inputs
nodes.description: SAR ADC Differential Inputs, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Phase-current shunt amplifiers must scale to 0-1.8 V window and keep pair matched and short (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-lite-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: DG32-2DOM SoC
nodes.description: DG32-2DOM SoC, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Adds an INT8 attention accelerator on clk_fast_i (114 MHz) with 2-flop CDC bridges to the 50 MHz CPU domain so attention compute never stalls the frozen control core. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-datasheets-qfn64.pdf)

nodes.name: DG32-LITE SoC
nodes.description: DG32-LITE SoC, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-datasheets-qfn64.pdf)

nodes.description: DShot ESC Engine (0xC000_0000), DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-datasheets-qfn64.pdf)

nodes.name: INT8 Attention Engine (0xE000_0000)
nodes.description: INT8 Attention Engine (0xE000_0000), DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Runs on clk_fast_i (114 MHz) and reaches memory through CDC bridges so as not to stall the 50 MHz CPU; supports SKIP_LOAD to reuse EXP/K/V buffers across kicks. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-datasheets-qfn64.pdf)

nodes.name: QFN-64 Board & Pin Interface
nodes.description: QFN-64 Board & Pin Interface, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. TMS/TDI are weakly pulled up and TCK weakly pulled down on-die so an unconnected JTAG header will not disturb the part. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-datasheets-qfn64.pdf)

nodes.name: SAR ADC (0xDB)
nodes.description: SAR ADC (0xDB), DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. Macro trim/clkc/comp taps were left unrouted because routing them made the die unroutable; register fields are retained for API stability. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-datasheets-qfn64.pdf)

nodes.name: DG32-2DOM SoC
nodes.description: DG32-2DOM SoC, DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. The DG32-LITE motor-control SoC plus an INT8 attention accelerator on a second clock domain (clk_fast_i at 114 MHz) with 2-flop CDC bridges so it never stalls the frozen control core. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: Board Design Guidance (Hardware / PCB)
nodes.description: Board Design Guidance (Hardware / PCB), DG32 RISC-V SoC Architecture. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-lite-preliminary-datasheet.pdf)

nodes.name: DGridRiscV Lockstep CPU Core
nodes.description: DGridRiscV Lockstep CPU Core, D100 UAV SoC Architecture. Runs at 50 MHz core domain; redundant checker core uses private 16 KB DMEM to prevent single physical defect from corrupting both cores identically (from dr/public/downloads/deepgrid-2dom-architecture.md)

nodes.name: Hardware Geometric EKF VIO Engine
nodes.description: Hardware Geometric EKF VIO Engine, D100 UAV SoC Architecture. Performs pure geometric localization to enable autonomous return-to-base without GNSS or magnetic compass under EW conditions (from dr/public/downloads/deepgrid-d100-architecture.md)

nodes.name: RV32IMC DGridRiscV Lockstep Core
nodes.description: RV32IMC DGridRiscV Lockstep Core, D100 UAV SoC Architecture. Redundant checker core uses private 16 KB DMEM so a single physical memory defect cannot corrupt both cores identically. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-2dom-architecture.md)

nodes.name: Hardware Geometric EKF VIO Engine
nodes.description: Hardware Geometric EKF VIO Engine, D100 UAV SoC Architecture. Hardwired matrix math solving 6-DoF pose at 30 Hz to maintain <0.8% drift under contested zero-GNSS/jammed environments. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-d100-architecture.md)

nodes.name: Hardware Failsafe Island (Hardware Wedge)
nodes.description: Hardware Failsafe Island (Hardware Wedge), D100 UAV SoC Architecture. 100% isolated power/clock island with pure RTL state machine and pad MUX that overrides processors and drives ESCs during link loss or software lockup. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-d100-architecture.md)

nodes.name: Dual DGridRiscV Flight Core (RV32IM_Safety)
nodes.description: Dual DGridRiscV Flight Core (RV32IM_Safety), D100 UAV SoC Architecture. Executes exclusively out of 512 KB zero-wait-state tightly-coupled SRAM with ECC to eliminate non-deterministic cache-miss jitter. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-d100-architecture.md)

nodes.name: 4-Layer Organic SiP Substrate
nodes.description: 4-Layer Organic SiP Substrate, D100 UAV SoC Architecture. Deliberately chosen over UCIe/silicon interposers to avoid offshore packaging reliance and cut NRE from >$1.5M to <$35k (from dr/public/downloads/deepgrid-d100-architecture.md)

nodes.name: Heterogeneous Organic SiP Packaging
nodes.description: Heterogeneous Organic SiP Packaging, D100 UAV SoC Architecture. Deliberately rejects UCIe or silicon interposers to avoid offshore advanced foundry dependencies and reduce NRE from >$1.5M to <$35k. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-d100-architecture.md)

nodes.name: DeepGrid D100 UAV Brain
nodes.description: DeepGrid D100 UAV Brain, D100 UAV SoC Architecture. System-in-Package engineered on a 4-layer organic BGA substrate rejecting UCIe/silicon interposers to eliminate offshore dependency and high packaging NRE. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-d100-architecture.md)

nodes.name: dgrid_dshot_rx Module
nodes.description: dgrid_dshot_rx Module, DG32-LITE Motor Diagnostics. Per-channel RX decoder containing 2-FF synchronizer, glitch filter, high-time counter, shift register, and CRC4 engine (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dshot-rx-architecture.md)

nodes.name: dgrid_dshot_tel Module
nodes.description: dgrid_dshot_tel Module, DG32-LITE Motor Diagnostics. Per-channel telemetry reply engine handling CRC, GCR 4b/5b, and transition encoding with early abort on collision (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dshot-rx-architecture.md)

nodes.name: dgrid_lockstep_check
nodes.description: dgrid_lockstep_check, DG32-LITE Motor Diagnostics. Trails the main core by 2 cycles; requires write-1-to-clear status flags to avoid desynchronization from read side-effects (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dshot-rx-architecture.md)

nodes.name: 8-Bin Goertzel Recurrence Filter
nodes.description: 8-Bin Goertzel Recurrence Filter, DG32-LITE Motor Diagnostics. Replaces standard 2^20-point FFT requiring 8 MB RAM with 6,144 cycles and 0.7 KB RAM evaluated strictly at predicted physical sideband frequencies (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-ai-architecture.md)

nodes.name: Hardware Safety Isolation Gate (ISO 26262 ASIL-D)
nodes.description: Hardware Safety Isolation Gate (ISO 26262 ASIL-D), DG32-LITE Motor Diagnostics. ML classifiers operate in advisory-only roles; hard trip limits are strictly held by secondary hardware comparator to assert FAULTn within 2 clock cycles bypassing software (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-ai-architecture.md)

nodes.name: Dual-Core Lockstep RV32IM CPU
nodes.description: Dual-Core Lockstep RV32IM CPU, DG32-LITE Motor Diagnostics. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-ai-architecture.md)

nodes.name: Pad-Ring Bridge Safety Configuration
nodes.description: Pad-Ring Bridge Safety Configuration, DG32-LITE Motor Diagnostics. High-side PWM pads are reused as PC_BIDIR for DShot RX, while low-side PWM pads remain untouched PC_OUT to prevent half-bridge shoot-through (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dshot-rx-architecture.md)

nodes.name: SRAM Architecture 28 KB vs 32 KB Floorplan
nodes.shortName: sram architecture 28 kb vs 32 kb floorplan
nodes.description: SRAM Architecture 28 KB vs 32 KB Floorplan, DG32-LITE Motor Diagnostics. 28 KB layout reduces SRAM macro rows from 7 to 6, doubling available logic strip area from 1.75 mm² to 3.40 mm² to avoid placement routing congestion in 2DOM (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dshot-rx-architecture.md)

nodes.name: DG32-LITE Edge AI & Predictive Diagnostics System Architecture
nodes.shortName: dg32-lite edge ai & predictive diagnostics system architecture
nodes.description: DG32-LITE Edge AI & Predictive Diagnostics System Architecture, DG32-LITE Motor Diagnostics. High-accuracy industrial condition monitoring and predictive diagnostics on a 50 MHz scalar core by exploiting zero-multiplication tree ensembles rather than heavy transformer or NPU acceleration (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-ai-architecture.md)

nodes.name: Clock-Domain Bridges
nodes.description: Clock-Domain Bridges, DG32 Clock and Subsystems. Crossings are rare, so a small, provably safe four-phase level handshake beats a FIFO with gray-coded pointers. (from dr/source/dg32-architecture/dg32-2dom-architecture.md)

nodes.name: 114 MHz Compute Domain
nodes.description: 114 MHz Compute Domain, DG32 Clock and Subsystems. Dedicated clock domain for INT8 attention engine allows high-throughput condition monitoring without starving the safety-critical 50 MHz control core. (from dr/source/dg32-architecture/dg32-2dom-architecture.md)

nodes.name: 50 MHz Control Domain
nodes.description: 50 MHz Control Domain, DG32 Clock and Subsystems. Lockstep core tops out around 55-62 MHz, so the control domain stays at 50 MHz to ensure timing closure is never disturbed. (from dr/source/dg32-architecture/dg32-2dom-architecture.md)

nodes.name: Bus, System, and Test
nodes.description: Bus, System, and Test, DG32 Clock and Subsystems. Unmapped addresses return bus errors via an error slave because hung bus transactions on a debugger-less chip would brick it. (from dr/source/dg32-architecture/dg32-lite-architecture.md)

nodes.name: Memory and Boot Subsystem
nodes.description: Memory and Boot Subsystem, DG32 Clock and Subsystems. Flash-less die keeps the 130 nm process simple, booting from mask ROM into SRAM from external QSPI flash. (from dr/source/dg32-architecture/dg32-lite-architecture.md)

nodes.name: Motor Drive Subsystem (PWM & DShot)
nodes.description: Motor Drive Subsystem (PWM & DShot), DG32 Clock and Subsystems. Gate timing and safety braking are too critical for software loops; hardware brake cuts outputs within two clock cycles. (from dr/source/dg32-architecture/dg32-lite-architecture.md)

nodes.name: Dual-Core Lockstep Safety Core
nodes.description: Dual-Core Lockstep Safety Core, DG32 Clock and Subsystems. A silent CPU datapath fault can produce a wrong PWM edge and destroy a power bridge; two cores with a comparator catch datapath faults in hardware at fixed latency rather than relying on periodic software self-test. (from dr/source/dg32-architecture/dg32-lite-architecture.md)

nodes.name: Hardware CORDIC Engine
nodes.description: Hardware CORDIC Engine, DG32 Bearing Fault Subsystem. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-2dom-architecture.md)

nodes.name: VexiiRiscv rv32imc Core Pair

nodes.name: AVIP Bearing-Fault Classifier

nodes.name: Goertzel Recurrence Filter

nodes.name: Hardware Safety Isolation Gate
nodes.description: Hardware Safety Isolation Gate, DG32-LITE Edge AI Architecture. ML diagnostic classifiers operate in advisory role only; all hard trips assert FAULTn within 2 clock cycles via hardware comparator core to meet ISO 26262 ASIL-D. (from dr/public/downloads/deepgrid-dg32-ai-architecture.md)

nodes.name: DG32 QFN-64 Pad-Ring Direction Mux
nodes.description: DG32 QFN-64 Pad-Ring Direction Mux, DG32-LITE Edge AI Architecture. Reuses PWM high-side pads (PC_BIDIR) while leaving low-side pads untouched (PC_OUT) strictly to prevent bridge shoot-through. (from dr/public/downloads/deepgrid-dshot-rx-architecture.md)

nodes.description: DG32-LITE Edge AI Architecture, DG32-LITE Edge AI Architecture. nodes.description: Field-Oriented Control Loop Flow, Field-Oriented Motor Control Hardware. Ensures deterministic ~300-cycle fixed hardware execution per current loop, leaving sufficient CPU budget for regulators up to 100 kHz. (from dr/public/downloads/dg32-lite-architecture-guide.md)

nodes.name: Motor Drive Peripherals

nodes.name: Lockstep Safety Core
nodes.description: Lockstep Safety Core, Field-Oriented Motor Control Hardware. (from dr/public/downloads/dg32-lite-architecture-guide.md)

nodes.name: Sensing and Math Hardware

nodes.name: Boot ROM (dgrid_imem_rom_macro)

nodes.name: Fault CSR (dgrid_fault_csr, 0xD6)

nodes.name: Interrupt Controller (dgrid_irq, 0xDF)

nodes.name: Supervisor & Windowed WDT (dg_supervisor, 0xD7)

nodes.description: DG32-LITE Microcontroller, DG32 Memory and Pinout. (from dr/public/downloads/deepgrid-datasheets-engineering-spec.md)

nodes.name: dgrid_adc (0xDB)
nodes.description: dgrid_adc (0xDB), DG32 Core Peripheral RTL. On-die ADC avoids ~1.9 us SPI read latency in ~5 us FOC loop, using simple start pulse and poll. Macro trim/clkc/comp pins are left open because routing them inside met1-3 obstructions makes die unroutable. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: dgrid_axi_cdc
nodes.description: dgrid_axi_cdc, DG32 Core Peripheral RTL. 4-phase level handshake with 2-FF synchronisers is small, provably safe, and avoids gray-coded pointers for low transaction rate; burst variants batch entire read/write bursts to eliminate per-beat crossing cost. Allows engine to run faster than 50 MHz CPU domain without touching frozen core timing closure. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: dgrid_cordic (0xDE)
nodes.description: dgrid_cordic (0xDE), DG32 Core Peripheral RTL. Park/Clarke transforms need sin/cos every control tick; a software trig call would dominate the loop, whereas fixed-latency CORDIC makes transform cost known. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: dgrid_dma
nodes.description: dgrid_dma, DG32 Core Peripheral RTL. DMA plus idle SRAM read port moves blocks for attention feed and sensor buffering without burning CPU copy cycles while CPU performs control math. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: dgrid_dshot (0xC0000000)
nodes.description: dgrid_dshot (0xC0000000), DG32 Core Peripheral RTL. Pad-muxed onto PWM pads because an output is either analog complementary PWM leg or digital DShot line, giving choice at boot without spending package balls. Placed at 0xC0000000 because 0xD0-0xDF peripheral block was full, bit 31 set passes CPU PMA whitelist. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: dgrid_int8_attn
nodes.description: dgrid_int8_attn, DG32 Core Peripheral RTL. INT8 with u15 weights into 40-bit numerator avoids 1/400 softmax weight rounding to zero seen in INT4 and int32 overflow at NK=512. Loading K/V once and re-reading keeps per-head bus traffic at ~1% instead of 400x streaming. Engine is on clk_fast_i to exceed 50 MHz without dragging frozen CPU timing. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: dgrid_pwm (0xD8)
nodes.description: dgrid_pwm (0xD8), DG32 Core Peripheral RTL. Center-aligned PWM puts the current-sampling instant at the ripple null so ADC reads true phase current without an analog filter delay. Hardware brake path is combinational to gates and sticky because firmware is too slow during bridge faults. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: VexiiRiscv Lockstep Core
nodes.description: VexiiRiscv Lockstep Core, DG32 Core Peripheral RTL. FetchCachelessPlugin core is fetch-bound (~8 cycles/instruction from SRAM), driving design decision to offload loop-critical FOC operations (Park/Clarke transform, current sampling, PWM) to hardware blocks (CORDIC, SAR ADC, PWM). (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: dgrid_adc (SAR ADC Macro & Wrapper)
nodes.description: dgrid_adc (SAR ADC Macro & Wrapper), AVIP Current Signature Analysis. Macro trim/clkc/comp taps are walled inside metal and left unrouted due to routability constraints, so ADC runs untrimmed while fields are kept for API stability. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: dgrid_dshot (DShot ESC Engine)
nodes.description: dgrid_dshot (DShot ESC Engine), AVIP Current Signature Analysis. Pin-muxed onto the PWM pads, generating 16-bit DShot frames across 4 channels sharing one bit-time counter. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: dgrid_fault_csr (Fault CSR)
nodes.description: dgrid_fault_csr (Fault CSR), AVIP Current Signature Analysis. Holds poison and first cause sticky across continued execution; matched lockstep-compare event counter. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: dgrid_int8_attn (INT8 Attention Engine)
nodes.description: dgrid_int8_attn (INT8 Attention Engine), AVIP Current Signature Analysis. Accelerates self-attention and cross-attention blocks (softmax(QK^T)V per head); operates on clk_fast_i so inference does not steal cycles from the 50 MHz control core. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: dgrid_irq (IRQ Aggregator)
nodes.description: dgrid_irq (IRQ Aggregator), AVIP Current Signature Analysis. Aggregates interrupts from 9 sources (TMR0/1, PWM trig, ADC done, DMA done, I2C done, FAULT, SW, ATTN). (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: dgrid_pwm (3-Phase PWM)
nodes.description: dgrid_pwm (3-Phase PWM), AVIP Current Signature Analysis. 3-phase center-aligned PWM with shadow duty latching and async hardware brake. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: fw/avip_csa (Current Signature Analysis Front End)
nodes.description: fw/avip_csa (Current Signature Analysis Front End), AVIP Current Signature Analysis. Samples phase current via SAR ADC at PWM ripple null to extract carrier + AM envelope, avoiding the need for an external accelerometer. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: AVIP Bearing-Fault Detection Model
nodes.description: AVIP Bearing-Fault Detection Model, AVIP Current Signature Analysis. INT8 multimodal bearing-fault classifier combining time and FFT branches fused via self-attention and cross-attention blocks. (from dr/public/downloads/docs/deepgrid-dg32-2dom-system-architecture.pdf)

nodes.name: Tree Ensembles & The 19-Model Hierarchy
nodes.communityName: 30 Industrial Edge AI Use Cases & Scalar DSP
nodes.description: Why zero-multiply decision trees and linear models outperform deep neural networks on microcontrollers. On a scalar CPU without a MAC array, comparisons and table lookups cost almost nothing. A 100-tree random forest at depth 8 requires roughly 800 comparisons and zero multiplications, running in 0.06 ms at >1 kHz.

nodes.name: Feature Extraction & CORDIC Demodulation
nodes.communityName: 30 Industrial Edge AI Use Cases & Scalar DSP
nodes.description: Costed signal-processing front-end: envelope demodulation, Goertzel filters, and kurtosis rules. The diagnostic front-end reuses CORDIC hardware already present for motor control (Park/Clarke/magnitude/atan2 in <20 cycles). Demodulated features evaluated at known physical fault frequencies outrank raw moments by 4–5×.
nodes.citation: DG32-LITE Base Variant: Thirty Use Cases, No Accelerator, Slide 06

nodes.name: AFE Sensing Constraints & ISO Standards
nodes.communityName: Deterministic Motor Control & Lockstep Safety RTL
nodes.description: Why the analog front end, not compute or RAM, is the true binding constraint in motor diagnostics. ISO 13373-2 defines usable dynamic range as D = 6(N-1) dB. For an 8-bit ADC, dynamic range is only 42 dB, while broken rotor bar sidebands sit -40 to -60 dBc below the fundamental, disappearing under the quantization floor.
nodes.citation: DG32-LITE Base Variant: Thirty Use Cases, No Accelerator, Slide 11

nodes.name: CWRU Benchmark Audit & Advisory ML Boundary
nodes.communityName: Deterministic Motor Control & Lockstep Safety RTL
nodes.description: Academic data leakage audit and the strict advisory role of machine learning under hardware lockstep. A critical audit of academic bearing benchmarks reveals widespread data leakage: 40 of 41 published CWRU studies used leaky splits. Furthermore, ML inference on DG32-LITE operates in an advisory role only, subservient to the lockstep safety core.

nodes.description: One 57 mm² die with six compute domains under all fifteen products. TSMC 28nm monolithic SoC2. A 57mm² die with six compute domains: A100 neural processing, R100 radar DSP, T100 AI, D100 security, S100 vehicle control and H100 monitoring. 39.3 TOPS is derived architecture arithmetic, not measured silicon performance. Eleven sensor channels have an 8.6 ms fusion design target in a 33.3 ms frame.

chunks.text: DG32-LITE - Preliminary Datasheet Deepgrid Semi Pvt Ltd - preliminary, confidential Page 1 DEEPGRID SEMI PVT LTD - PRELIMINARY DATASHEET DG32-LITE - Preliminary Datasheet Lockstep RISC-V motor-control SoC on SkyWater sky130A, in a 64-pin QFN. Dual rv32imc cores with a fault comparator, 32 KB SRAM, 64 KB self-boot ROM and QSPI-XIP, a 3-phase motor peripheral set (PWM, DShot, encoder, CORDIC, on-die SAR ADC) and UART/SPI/I2C/GPIO. For firmware and hardware/PCB engineers. Part Package Process Core Clock DG32-LITE QFN-64, 9x9 mm sky130A 130 nm 2x rv32imc lockstep 50 MHz Preliminary, pre-silicon. Functional and register detail is from the taped-out RTL and the hardened die. Electrical limits are design targets and sky130 process nominals pending first-silicon characterisation, and are marked where they are not yet measured. The flight-control core is frozen until silicon test. 1 Features • Dual DGridRiscV rv32imc cores in lockstep with a cycle-by-cycle fault comparator and a sticky fault CSR. • 32 KB on-chip SRAM (no ECC); 64 KB baked boot ROM; QSPI execute-in-place window for external NOR flash. • 3-phase center-aligned complementary PWM with programmable dead-time and a hardware brake. • 4-channel DShot ESC engine, pin-muxed onto the PWM output pads. • Quadrature + Hall encoder with edge timestamps; CORDIC (sin/cos, atan2, magnitude) for field-oriented control. • On-die 8-bit differential SAR ADC for phase-current feedback, PWM-triggered. • Two UARTs, an SPI master, a 7-bit I2C master, 14-pin GPIO, two timers, a windowed watchdog and rail supervisor. • Interrupt controller; standalone self-boot (no management core); SLVERR on any unmapped access. • Single 50 MHz clock domain; whole die powered from a 1.8 V rail; 3.3 V I/O. 2 Pinout - 64-pin QFN (top view)

DG32-LITE - Preliminary Datasheet Deepgrid Semi Pvt Ltd - preliminary, confidential Page 6 6 Clock, reset and boot 6.1 Clock and reset A single core clock enters on CLK (pin 31), 3.3 V CMOS, 50 MHz design target. There is no on-die PLL. Two reset inputs are ANDed on die: the OpenFrame harness resetb (pin 21, active low) and RST_N (pin 28, active low); either may be used, pull the unused one high. The DG32-LITE die runs entirely from this one 50 MHz domain. 6.2 Boot flow The die is standalone - no management core. At power-on the on-die 64 KB boot ROM runs with no external help: • Emit the boot banner on UART0 (pin 42) at 115200 8N1 (baud divider fixed for 50 MHz). • Read the QSPI NOR flash header through the 0x1 window (boot magic 0xD632_B007, then length). • Copy the flash image into SRAM over the QSPI quad-output-fast-read (0x6B, 1-1-4, 8 dummy cycles, SCLK = clk/2). • Jump to the copied image and run from SRAM/ROM. • A UART monitor (r/w/j/i commands) is available if the flash is blank, so a bare board is still inspectable. Instruction fetch is ROM-only. The CPU fetch bus is wired to the boot ROM alone. The QSPI-XIP window and SRAM are reachable by loads and stores, not by instruction fetch - code does not execute in place from external NOR, it is copied to SRAM first. Firmware and linker scripts must place executable code in SRAM.

DG32-LITE - Preliminary Datasheet Deepgrid Semi Pvt Ltd - preliminary, confidential Page 7 7 Memory map Base-address decode from the top-level decoder: selector is addr[31:28]; the 0xD page sub-decodes addr[27:24], so each 0xD peripheral base is 0xDX00_0000. Any unmapped access completes with SLVERR (it never hangs the bus). Base Block Note 0x1000_0000 QSPI-XIP read window data read window (loads); NOT instruction fetch 0x9000_0000 SRAM 32 KB main data memory 0xC000_0000 DShot ESC engine pin-muxed onto the PWM pads 0xD000_0000 UART0 console / boot banner 0xD100_0000 UART1 telemetry 0xD200_0000 SPI master 0xD300_0000 GPIO 14 pins on the die 0xD400_0000 TIMER0 0xD500_0000 TIMER1 0xD600_0000 Fault CSR poison + cause 0xD700_0000 Supervisor / wWDT 0xD800_0000 PWM 3-phase center-aligned 0xD900_0000 I2C master 0xDA00_0000 Encoder quadrature + Hall 0xDB00_0000 SAR ADC 8-bit differential 0xDC00_0000 DMA 0xDD00_0000 SYSCTL device ID / clock gate 0xDE00_0000 CORDIC Q1.31 0xDF00_0000 IRQ aggregator Address constraint (firmware). The CPU has a hardwired PMA whitelist: a load or store is legal only if addr[31] is set or the address is in 0x1xxx_xxxx. That is why SRAM is at 0x9 and the peripherals at 0xC/0xD. An access outside the whitelist faults inside the CPU before the bus sees it.

DG32-LITE - Preliminary Datasheet Deepgrid Semi Pvt Ltd - preliminary, confidential Page 10 SAR ADC (0xDB) Offset Name R/W Bits / meaning 0x00 CTRL R/W [0]=enable; [1]=cal; [31:16]=clkdiv (reset 24 -> 50 MHz/25 = 2 MHz) 0x04 START W any write starts one conversion when enabled and not busy 0x08 RESULT R [7:0]=last conversion; [8]=valid (cleared on START) 0x0C STATUS R [0]=busy; [1]=valid; [2]=comp (raw comparator) 0x10 TRIM R/W [4:0]=trim bits (reset 01111). NOTE: no effect on silicon - see block note 8-bit differential SAR hard macro (1.8 V, on vccd1). ~200 kSa/s at the reset divider. The macro's trim/clkc/comp taps are walled inside its own metal and are left unrouted (routing them makes the die unroutable), so TRIM and CLKC have no effect on this silicon and STATUS.comp reads 0 - the ADC runs untrimmed. The register fields are kept for API stability. DG32-LITE - Preliminary Datasheet Deepgrid Semi Pvt Ltd - preliminary, confidential Page 12 9 Board design guidance (hardware / PCB) • Motor half-bridge gate driver on PWM_AH..CL (pins 3-8); the outputs are complementary with programmable dead-time. Respect the driver's shoot-through spec; the die also has a hardware brake that forces all six low. • Route PWM_TRIG (pin 11) to nothing external unless you want the ADC-sample instant on a test point; it fires at the centre-aligned current-ripple null. • Wire the encoder A/B/Z (pins 12-14) and Hall A/B/C (pins 15,16,22) directly; inputs are 2-flop synchronised and 3.3 V. • SAR ADC inputs ADC_VINP (62) and ADC_VINN (2) are differential, 0 to 1.8 V - scale phase-current shunt amplifiers into that window and keep the pair matched and short. • QSPI NOR boot flash on pins 32-37 (add CSN1=41 for a second device / PSRAM); a 3.3 V W25Q / S25FL works. Without a flash the ROM drops to the UART monitor. • I2C_SCL (53) and I2C_SDA (54) are open-drain - the carrier must supply the pull-ups (typ 2.2-4.7 k to 3.3 V). • Bring UART0 (42/43) to a USB-UART for the boot banner and console; UART1 (44/45) is free for telemetry. • FAULT_N (59) is an active-low fault output from the lockstep/supervisor - route it to the driver enable or a supervisor for a hardware trip. • Provide 3.3 V and 1.8 V per Section 5; the 100 production parts need a carrier with the 64-pin QFN footprint (KiCad from chipfoundry/caravel_board), gate drives, encoder, an optional external SPI ADC, and UART/JTAG headers. JTAG idles safely with no probe. TMS (pin 25) and TDI (pin 26) are weakly pulled up on die, TCK (pin 24) weakly pulled down, so an unconnected JTAG header will not disturb the part.

DG32-2DOM - Preliminary Datasheet Deepgrid Semi Pvt Ltd - preliminary, confidential Page 1 DEEPGRID SEMI PVT LTD - PRELIMINARY DATASHEET DG32-2DOM - Preliminary Datasheet The DG32-LITE motor-control SoC plus an INT8 attention accelerator on a second clock. Same lockstep core, boot path and motor peripheral set; adds a memory-mapped attention engine (0xE000_0000) that runs on clk_fast_i and reaches memory through clock-domain-crossing bridges. For firmware and hardware/PCB engineers. Part Package Process Core Clocks DG32-2DOM QFN-64, 9x9 mm sky130A 130 nm 2x rv32imc + INT8 attn 50 / 114 MHz Preliminary, pre-silicon. Functional and register detail is from the taped-out RTL and the hardened die. Electrical limits are design targets and sky130 process nominals pending first-silicon characterisation, and are marked where they are not yet measured. The flight-control core is frozen until silicon test. 1 Features • Everything in DG32-LITE: dual rv32imc lockstep core, 32 KB SRAM, 64 KB boot ROM, QSPI-XIP, and the full motor peripheral set (PWM, DShot, encoder, CORDIC, SAR ADC) plus UART/SPI/I2C/GPIO. • INT8 attention accelerator (0xE000_0000): one kick computes a band of query rows of one head end to end (QK^T, softmax/EXP, E.V, requantise to int8), bit-exact to the golden model. • Attention datapath: shared LANES-wide MAC array, 256-entry u15 EXP table, 40-bit numerator (exact to NK=131072), one reciprocal per row; ~3242 cycles/row analytic at LANES=16. • Second clock domain: the engine runs on clk_fast_i (114 MHz) and crosses to the 50 MHz CPU domain through 2-flop CDC bridges, so it never stalls the frozen control core. • Own die (3400 x 4500 um) with the attention K/V buffers on sky130 SRAM macros next to the SAR analog corner. 2 Pinout - 64-pin QFN (top view)

DG32-2DOM - Preliminary Datasheet Deepgrid Semi Pvt Ltd - preliminary, confidential Page 6 6 Clock, reset and boot 6.1 Clock and reset A single core clock enters on CLK (pin 31), 3.3 V CMOS, 50 MHz design target. There is no on-die PLL. Two reset inputs are ANDed on die: the OpenFrame harness resetb (pin 21, active low) and RST_N (pin 28, active low); either may be used, pull the unused one high. DG32-2DOM adds a second clock, clk_fast_i (114 MHz), for the attention engine; the CPU and all peripherals stay in the 50 MHz domain and the two are bridged by CDC logic. 6.2 Boot flow The die is standalone - no management core. At power-on the on-die 64 KB boot ROM runs with no external help: • Emit the boot banner on UART0 (pin 42) at 115200 8N1 (baud divider fixed for 50 MHz). • Read the QSPI NOR flash header through the 0x1 window (boot magic 0xD632_B007, then length). • Copy the flash image into SRAM over the QSPI quad-output-fast-read (0x6B, 1-1-4, 8 dummy cycles, SCLK = clk/2). • Jump to the copied image and run from SRAM/ROM. • A UART monitor (r/w/j/i commands) is available if the flash is blank, so a bare board is still inspectable. Instruction fetch is ROM-only. The CPU fetch bus is wired to the boot ROM alone. The QSPI-XIP window and SRAM are reachable by loads and stores, not by instruction fetch - code does not execute in place from external NOR, it is copied to SRAM first. Firmware and linker scripts must place executable code in SRAM.

The flight-control core is frozen until silicon test. 1 Features • Everything in DG32-LITE: dual rv32imc lockstep core, 32 KB SRAM, 64 KB boot ROM, QSPI-XIP, and the full motor peripheral set (PWM, DShot, encoder, CORDIC, SAR ADC) plus UART/SPI/I2C/GPIO. • INT8 attention accelerator (0xE000_0000): one kick computes a band of query rows of one head end to end (QK^T, softmax/EXP, E.V, requantise to int8), bit-exact to the golden model. • Attention datapath: shared LANES-wide MAC array, 256-entry u15 EXP table, 40-bit numerator (exact to NK=131072), one reciprocal per row; ~3242 cycles/row analytic at LANES=16. • Second clock domain: the engine runs on clk_fast_i (114 MHz) and crosses to the 50 MHz CPU domain through 2-flop CDC bridges, so it never stalls the frozen control core. • Own die (3400 x 4500 um) with the attention K/V buffers on sky130 SRAM macros next to the SAR analog corner. 2 Pinout - 64-pin QFN (top view)

DG32-2DOM - Preliminary Datasheet Deepgrid Semi Pvt Ltd - preliminary, confidential Page 6 6 Clock, reset and boot 6.1 Clock and reset A single core clock enters on CLK (pin 31), 3.3 V CMOS, 50 MHz design target. There is no on-die PLL. Two reset inputs are ANDed on die: the OpenFrame harness resetb (pin 21, active low) and RST_N (pin 28, active low); either may be used, pull the unused one high. DG32-2DOM adds a second clock, clk_fast_i (114 MHz), for the attention engine; the CPU and all peripherals stay in the 50 MHz domain and the two are bridged by CDC logic. 6.2 Boot flow The die is standalone - no management core. At power-on the on-die 64 KB boot ROM runs with no external help: • Emit the boot banner on UART0 (pin 42) at 115200 8N1 (baud divider fixed for 50 MHz). • Read the QSPI NOR flash header through the 0x1 window (boot magic 0xD632_B007, then length). • Copy the flash image into SRAM over the QSPI quad-output-fast-read (0x6B, 1-1-4, 8 dummy cycles, SCLK = clk/2). • Jump to the copied image and run from SRAM/ROM. • A UART monitor (r/w/j/i commands) is available if the flash is blank, so a bare board is still inspectable. Instruction fetch is ROM-only. The CPU fetch bus is wired to the boot ROM alone. The QSPI-XIP window and SRAM are reachable by loads and stores, not by instruction fetch - code does not execute in place from external NOR, it is copied to SRAM first. Firmware and linker scripts must place executable code in SRAM.

DG32-2DOM - System Architecture Deepgrid Semi Pvt Ltd - confidential Page 24 11 Application: AVIP bearing-fault detection The DG32-2DOM attention engine exists to run models like AVIP, an INT8 bearing-fault classifier (dgrid-a8w8). AVIP is multimodal - a time branch and an FFT branch, each a small conv stack plus a gated recurrent cell - fused by two self-attention blocks and one cross-attention block, ending in a per-class head. Those attention blocks are exactly what the engine accelerates. The shipped CWRU-trained model is 47,076 parameters at 94-95% held-out-load accuracy with INT8 equal to FP32; the full AVIP topology is 478,277 parameters. Both map onto the same op set with no new RTL. 11.1 What runs on the attention engine Model stage What it is DG32-2DOM mapping Self-attention (sa, sb) QKV projection + softmax(QK^T)V per head K_ATTN -> dgrid_int8_attn Cross-attention (cx) time<->freq fusion, one head set K_ATTN -> dgrid_int8_attn Head dimension key_dim 16 -> KD=16 multiple of LANES=16, within KDMAX=32 - fits as built Kicks per inference 6 (CWRU model) / 12 (full AVIP) one kick per (window, head) Conv / elementwise / dense the rest of the graph K_CONV / K_ELEM / K_AGEMM on the INT8 tile 11.2 Inference budget (measured on the INT8 op-graph) Model Positions Kicks Conv cycles Time (ms) CWRU model (47K params) 143,377 228,229 3,794,371 46.7 Full AVIP (478K params) 169,821 231,657 4,429,355 54.5 AVIP has 10x the parameters but only 1.2x the compute: its capacity is in deeper, narrower layers at lower spatial resolution, and compute tracks positions, not parameter count. The engine runs on clk_fast_i, so the ~50 ms inference does not steal cycles from the 50 MHz control core. Footprint.

The AVIP arena is ~2.49 MB (weights, LUTs, activations), so the full model runs from external memory on the DG32-2DOM / a8w8 class part - not from the 32 KB on-chip SRAM. The on-chip attention engine and INT8 tile are shared; the model image and activations live off-chip. 11.3 Current-signature front end (no accelerometer) AVIP trains on two accelerometers (drive-end + fan-end). A motor-control die already has the sensor it needs: the phase-current SAR ADC. A bearing defect modulates the stator current at f_e +/- k*f_fault (Current Signature Analysis), so the current envelope carries the same fault signature. The front end (fw/avip_csa) samples the SAR ADC at the PWM ripple null, derives two channels from the one current (raw carrier + AM envelope), and produces both a standalone classical fault score and the AVIP INT8 recurrence tensor. Bearing-fault detection is therefore a concrete reason the attention variant exists, and it reuses the motor's own current sense.

0 2 · A L G O R I T H M C H O I C E Where a scalar core is strong The absence of a MAC array reverses the usual ranking. Comparisons and table lookups cost almost nothing here. Tree ensembles are the best accuracy per cycle on this part A 100-tree random forest at depth 8 is roughly 800 comparisons and no multiplies at all, 0.06 ms, supporting rates above 1 kHz. A neural network of comparable accuracy on bearing-fault or power-quality classification costs 50–500× more cycles. This is not a compromise made for the hardware. On the CWRU bearing benchmark a random forest over five time-domain features reaches 95.6 %, and cutting from nine features to five costs 0.1 %. A review of 42 papers finds SVM at 95–100 % against deep methods at 97–100 %, statistically indistinguishable. Model capacity is not the bottleneck on these tasks. Signal conditioning is. The ordering that follows First choice, tree ensembles, linear discriminants, PCA with Hotelling T², Mahalanobis distance. Sub-millisecond, kHz-capable, inspectable in the field. Second choice, small dense networks and autoencoders, where a nonlinear boundary genuinely earns its place. Still sub-millisecond. Reach for last, recurrent and convolutional models. A GRU at 2.95 ms and a 1D-CNN at 10.3 ms both fit, but only where the raw waveform carries something hand-built features miss. Design rule. Spend effort on band selection, envelope demodulation and operating-condition normalisation before spending it on model capacity. The CORDIC unit does Park, Clarke, magnitude and atan2 in hardware, so the diagnostic front end reuses what the control loop already computes. S T A G E C Y C L E S T I M E W H A T I T Y I E L D S 256-point real FFT 30,720 0.61 ms Band energies, spectral peaks, harmonic ratios 512-point real FFT 69,120 1.38 ms Finer resolution for gear-mesh and sideband work Envelope demodulation 5,000 0.10 ms CORDIC magnitude, 20 iterations, the bearing-fault front end Goertzel, 8 bins 6,144 0.12 ms Narrowband detection at predicted fault frequencies Statistical moments 7,000 0.14 ms RMS, kurtosis, crest factor, skew, ISO 20816 baseline Broadband RMS velocity 3,000 0.06 ms ISO 20816 severity zone A/B/C/D Haar wavelet, 256 samples 15,000 0.30 ms Time-frequency features for transient faults Park / Clarke transform 120 0.00 ms CORDIC, already computed by the control loop Decimation and band- pass 4,000 0.08 ms IIR biquads ahead of envelope or raw- waveform models Why this matters more than the model A published feature-ranking study across twelve features found demodulated features evaluated at the known fault frequency outrank raw statistical moments by a factor of 4–5. Hilbert-Huang amplitude at the outer-race frequency scored 225.9; peak-to-peak scored 51.8. That is the whole argument for spending cycles on envelope demodulation and band selection rather than on a larger classifier. The envelope chain is also cheap: band-pass, rectify, low-pass, decimate to 1–2 kS/s, then a modest FFT. Do the decimation before buffering and the working set never exceeds a few kB. One caution.

Kurtosis is non-monotonic, it peaks for incipient localised defects then falls as damage spreads and the signal becomes Gaussian. RMS is the opposite: stable and monotonic, but blind to early faults. Trend both; never alarm on kurtosis alone. 0 9 · C O N S T R A I N T What the sensing supports Compute is not the binding constraint on these thirty use cases. The analog front end is. The current-based use cases need more than 8 bits ISO 13373-2 gives usable dynamic range as D = 6(N−1) dB, so eight bits yields 42 dB. ISO 20958 states rotor-bar sidebands sit 100 to 1,000 times below the fundamental, −40 to −60 dBc. The entire diagnostic range sits at or below the quantisation floor. Broken rotor bar, eccentricity and inter-turn short detection need either analog fundamental suppression and gain ahead of the converter, or 12–16 bits. A second constraint compounds it. Sideband separation is 2·s·f₁, roughly 3 Hz at full load, 0.5 Hz at light load, so these use cases need 30–100 second records at stable load and speed with 0.01–0.05 Hz resolution. A 2²⁰-point FFT is 8 MB and does not fit. Use Goertzel evaluated at the predicted sideband frequencies, which is why the electrical use cases on slide 06 are costed that way and not with an FFT. Tier 1, one accelerometer The highest-value addition. Bearings are 44 % of motor failures and are the weakest fault class for current-only sensing; rotor bars, where current is strongest, are 8–10 %. Needs ≥5 kHz usable bandwidth, many low-cost MEMS parts roll off at 1–3 kHz, below the bearing resonance band, which makes envelope analysis useless. Mounting matters as much as the part: stud mounting per ISO 13373-1, not magnet or adhesive. Tier 2, three-phase current and voltage Unlocks negative-sequence detection of stator inter-turn shorts, instantaneous power signature analysis and Park's vector per ISO 20958 Annex A. Needs a multi-channel converter; the part currently has one differential channel.

What works today, unchanged Everything on slide 08 and most of slide 09, vibration-based classification, sensorless observation, plausibility checking, regime identification, anomaly scoring and duty tracking, runs on the sensing already present, because they depend on relative change rather than absolute small-signal resolution. From the design Core configuration, memory sizes, peripheral set and the CORDIC capability come from the DG32- LITE block diagrams dated 10 September 2026 and the consolidated capability assessment of 11 September 2026. The 16.5 KB and 29.5 KB model budgets and the 12.5 MMAC/s scalar rate are taken from that assessment. Derived Every latency, memory figure and maximum rate in this deck is calculated, feature- extraction cycles plus model cycles at 4 cycles per int8 multiply-accumulate, against 82 % of a 50 MHz core. That constant is back-solved from the design documents and has not been measured on silicon. One cycle- accurate measurement on run R firmware relocates every rate here. Third-party, verified 11 Sept 2026 CWRU random-forest accuracy and the 42-paper review, the twelve-feature ranking study, the kurtosis non-monotonicity result, and the ISO signal-processing limits were checked against primary sources, IEEE and MDPI papers, the PHM Society proceedings, and the ISO catalogue entries for 13373-1, 13373-2, 20958 and 20816- 3. On accuracy expectations Do not carry published bearing-benchmark accuracy into a specification. Forty of forty-one reviewed CWRU studies used splits vulnerable to data leakage; on a leakage-free bearing-wise split one classifier fell from 85.8 % to 69.5 %. Realistic accuracy on unseen physical bearings is 65–80 %. Smith and Randall further showed a meaningful fraction of CWRU records are not diagnosable by correct physics at all, which is why 99 % figures on that dataset should be treated as artefacts. What is not claimed No workload here has been compiled for or measured on DG32-LITE, which has not completed place-and-route.

No inference result carries a safety integrity claim, that architecture places the classifier in an advisory role with a lockstepped deterministic monitor holding the trip limits. Model choices are the appropriate algorithm for each task on this core, not trained and validated implementations. DG32-LITE - Preliminary Datasheet Deepgrid Semi Pvt Ltd - preliminary, confidential Page 6 6 Clock, reset and boot 6.1 Clock and reset A single core clock enters on CLK (pin 31), 3.3 V CMOS, 50 MHz design target. There is no on-die PLL. Two reset inputs are ANDed on die: the OpenFrame harness resetb (pin 21, active low) and RST_N (pin 28, active low); either may be used, pull the unused one high. The DG32-LITE die runs entirely from this one 50 MHz domain. 6.2 Boot flow The die is standalone - no management core. At power-on the on-die 64 KB boot ROM runs with no external help: • Emit the boot banner on UART0 (pin 42) at 115200 8N1 (baud divider fixed for 50 MHz). • Read the QSPI NOR flash header through the 0x1 window (boot magic 0xD632_B007, then length). • Copy the flash image into SRAM over the QSPI quad-output-fast-read (0x6B, 1-1-4, 8 dummy cycles, SCLK = clk/2). • Jump to the copied image and run from SRAM/ROM. • A UART monitor (r/w/j/i commands) is available if the flash is blank, so a bare board is still inspectable. Instruction fetch is ROM-only. The CPU fetch bus is wired to the boot ROM alone. The QSPI-XIP window and SRAM are reachable by loads and stores, not by instruction fetch - code does not execute in place from external NOR, it is copied to SRAM first. Firmware and linker scripts must place executable code in SRAM.

Without a flash the ROM drops to the UART monitor. • I2C_SCL (53) and I2C_SDA (54) are open-drain - the carrier must supply the pull-ups (typ 2.2-4.7 k to 3.3 V). • Bring UART0 (42/43) to a USB-UART for the boot banner and console; UART1 (44/45) is free for telemetry. • FAULT_N (59) is an active-low fault output from the lockstep/supervisor - route it to the driver enable or a supervisor for a hardware trip. • Provide 3.3 V and 1.8 V per Section 5; the 100 production parts need a carrier with the 64-pin QFN footprint (KiCad from chipfoundry/caravel_board), gate drives, encoder, an optional external SPI ADC, and UART/JTAG headers. dgrid_dshot_rx, DShot receive + bidirectional telemetry reply Block spec for review · DG32 · 13 Sep 2026 · draft 1 Author: DG32 engineering (drafted with Claude). Reviewer: Ayaz Khan. 0. Ayaz's questions, answered from the RTL # Question Answer Source 1 Do the timers at 0xD4/0xD5 have pin-routed input capture? No. dgrid_timer 's entire non-AXI interface is tick_o and irq_o . No input pin, no capture register. DShot300-via- timer is not an interim path. rtl/dgrid_timer.sv module ports 1b Is there any edge- timestamp hardware on the die? Yes, on the encoder. dgrid_encoder (0xDA) has a free-running 32-bit timestamp_q captured on Hall/quadrature edges ("Hall decode with edge timestamps"). It is functionally input- capture, bonded to the encoder/Hall pads, not the timers. rtl/dgrid_encoder.sv:26,91-95 2 Datasheet says 14 GPIO, pinout bonds 3, which is right? The pinout. NGPIO = 3 . It was 14; 11 pads were reclaimed for I²C (2) and scan/DFT (4). The datasheet is stale and must be corrected. rtl/dg32_lite_top.sv:149 3 28 KB vs 32 KB SRAM Both positions are legitimate and they answer different questions, see §9. The codex branch is already running both a 24 KB variant ( 2dom/12 ) and a keep-32 KB spread-floorplan test ( 2dom/13 ). Those runs decide it with data. autoresearch/configs/2dom/12,13 4 "DShot bidirectional / RPM telemetry, settled: not supported" Re-opened by this spec. Ayaz's case is correct: it cannot be done in firmware, and it is required for DG32-as-ESC. this document 1. Why firmware cannot do this (confirming Ayaz's argument) DShot600 is 1.67 µs/bit; the 0/1 decision is a high-time of 625 ns vs 1250 ns.

At 50 MHz that is 31 vs 62 cycles, so the decode needs ~±15-cycle (±300 ns) edge placement, achievable only by a busy-wait loop with interrupts off for the full 16-bit frame (~1,340 cycles at DShot600, ~2,700 at DShot300). That collides with: the 5 µs FOC loop (250 cycles), a single DShot frame is 5× longer than the entire control period;

the lockstep compare window, dgrid_lockstep_check compares every committed store; a firmware bit-bang that branches on pad reads produces store streams whose timing depends on an asynchronous input, which is exactly the class of behaviour the checker is designed to flag. And bidirectional reply is impossible in firmware regardless of speed: the ESC must turn the pad from input to output ~30 µs after the command frame ends and drive a 21-bit reply, the pad has no output-enable today. This is a pad-ring fact, not a software one. Conclusion: hardware RX + hardware reply, or no ESC role. 2. What exists today (baseline) dgrid_dshot (slot 0xC, rtl/dgrid_dshot.sv ) is transmit-only: 4 channels, one shared bit-time counter, per-channel 16-bit frame + CRC4, programmable BITPERIOD / T0H / T1H . Its only pins are output [3:0] dshot_o . The four channels reach the pads only through SYSCTL PINMUX[0] , which AND-ORs them onto the PWM high-side pads AH / BH / CH / SAMPLE_TRIG ( dg32_lite_top.sv:775-792 ). The low-side PWM pads are never muxed, so a mis-set mux cannot shoot through a bridge. Pad budget is 44/44 with zero spare. There is no pad for a receiver. The RX path therefore must reuse the same four pads, which means those pads become bidirectional. That is the single most consequential change in this spec (§7). 3. Protocol facts the design depends on 3.1 Command frame (FC → ESC), what RX decodes 16 bits, MSB first: [15:5] throttle (11 b) · [4] telemetry request · [3:0] CRC4.

Each bit is one pulse of fixed period; high-time encodes the value (long = 1, short = 0). speed bit period T0H T1H @50 MHz period / T0H / T1H (cycles) DShot150 6.67 µs 2.50 µs 5.00 µs 333 / 125 / 250 DShot300 3.33 µs 1.25 µs 2.50 µs 167 / 62 / 125 DShot600 1.67 µs 0.625 µs 1.25 µs 83 / 31 / 62 DShot1200 0.83 µs 0.312 µs 0.625 µs 42 / 16 / 31 CRC4, normal mode: crc = n0 ^ n1 ^ n2 of the 12-bit {throttle, telem}, identical to the TX engine's crc4_of() . CRC4, bidirectional mode: crc = ~(n0 ^ n1 ^ n2) & 0xF . The inverted CRC is how the protocol marks a bidirectional-capable frame. 3.2 Bidirectional mode signalling In bidirectional DShot the line is inverted: idle high, bits are low pulses (high-time above becomes low-time). The ESC recognises bidirectional mode from the inverted idle level and inverted CRC. RX needs an INVERT control bit that flips the input sense before the width measurement.

chunks.section: 3.3 Telemetry reply (ESC → FC), what the reply engine sends
chunks.text: 3.3 Telemetry reply (ESC → FC), what the reply engine sends The reply is not a DShot command frame, so it cannot reuse the TX engine's shifter unmodified: 1. Payload: 16 bits = [15:4] eRPM period (3-bit exponent e , 9-bit mantissa m ; period_µs = m << e ) · [3:0] CRC where crc = ~(v ^ v>>4 ^ v>>8) & 0xF over the 12-bit period field. 2. GCR 4b→5b encode each nibble (table: 19 1B 12 13 1D 15 16 17 1A 09 0A 0B 1E 0D 0E 0F ) → 20 bits. 3. Transition-encode to 21 bits: out[0] = 0; out[i] = out[i-1] ^ G[i-1], a 1 in the GCR stream is a level transition, not a level. 4. Transmit inverted, at 5/4 the command bit rate (DShot600 → 750 kbit/s, 1.33 µs/bit = 66.7 cycles), starting ~30 µs after the command frame's last edge. The FC decodes edges back with G = s ^ (s >> 1) . This is the Betaflight/Bluejay/AM32 convention; get any of the three steps wrong and every FC on the market reports CRC errors. 4. Architecture Recommendation: extend slot 0xC in place, not a new slot. The RX and reply engines are added inside dgrid_dshot as two self-contained sub-modules ( dgrid_dshot_rx , dgrid_dshot_tel ), sharing the existing AXI slave, the pad mux and the bit-timing registers.

chunks.section: 3.3 Telemetry reply (ESC → FC), what the reply engine sends
chunks.text: Reasons: (a) the address map has no free slot without touching the decoder and error-slave logic that is frozen for tape-in; (b) RX and TX are mutually exclusive on the same pads, so one owner of the pad direction is safer than two; (c) BITPERIOD/T0H/T1H already encode the speed class, RX derives its threshold from them by default. ┌───────────── dgrid_dshot (slot 0xC) ─────────────┐ AXI-lite ──────────►│ regs │ TX engine (existing) ───────────┐ │ │ │ │ mux/dir │──► pad_o[3:0] │ │ dgrid_dshot_tel (reply, GCR) ────┤ + OE │──► pad_oe[3:0] │ │ │ │ │ │ dgrid_dshot_rx ◄── sync/filter ◄┘ │◄── pad_i[3:0] │ └── irq_o │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Per channel (×4): RX decoder, reply shifter, direction FSM. Shared: bit-time counter (existing), threshold/timeout/turnaround registers, 2-FF synchronisers. 4.1 RX decoder (per channel) Input: pad_i → 2-FF synchroniser → 2-sample glitch filter → INVERT XOR → rx_level . Rising edge of rx_level starts a 12-bit high-time counter; falling edge stops it and compares to RXTHRESH : bit = (high_time > RXTHRESH) . 16-bit shift register, MSB first. A 4-bit bit counter completes the frame at 16. Frame boundary: an idle period longer than RXTIMEOUT cycles (default ≈ 2 × BITPERIOD) resets the bit counter, this is how a mid-frame glitch or a lost edge cannot desynchronise the receiver permanently. On 16 bits: compute CRC4 per §3.1 (mode-dependent), latch {throttle, telem} , set VALID ; set CRC_ERR instead if mismatch; set OVERRUN if VALID was still set (firmware hadn't read the previous frame).

Synchroniser + filter add a fixed 3-cycle (60 ns) latency to both edges, so measured width is unaffected. 4.2 Reply engine dgrid_dshot_tel (per channel) Armed when TELEM_EN=1 and a valid frame with telem=1 arrives (or TELEM_ALWAYS=1, bidirectional FCs expect a reply on every frame). Waits TURNAROUND cycles from the command frame's last edge, then asserts pad_oe , drives the 21-bit stream from TELEMn at TELEMPERIOD cycles/bit (inverted), then releases pad_oe and returns the pad to input. GCR + transition encoding (§3.3) done in hardware from the 12-bit period value firmware writes to TELEMn . Firmware supplies only {e, m} ; CRC, GCR and transition coding are hardware. This keeps the firmware side to one register write per commutation-period update. If a new command frame's first edge arrives while a reply is being driven, the reply is aborted and OE released within one cycle, never fight the FC for the wire. TEL_ABORT status bit is set. 4.3 Direction ownership pad_oe per channel is the OR of: TX engine BUSY (existing TX role, always drives) and dgrid_dshot_tel driving . In RX-only or RX+reply roles the TX engine is never started, so the pad idles as input. PINMUX[0] continues to select DShot vs PWM; PWM-role pads remain output- only (OE forced high) so the bridge-safety property is preserved. 5.

Register map (slot 0xC, addr[7:0] ; existing registers 0x00–0x20 unchanged) addr name bits R/W description 0x24 RXCTRL [0] RX_EN RW enable receivers (all 4 channels) [1] INVERT RW bidirectional-mode sense: idle high, low pulses, inverted CRC [2] TELEM_EN RW reply engine armed on frames with telem bit set [3] TELEM_ALWAYS RW reply on every valid frame regardless of telem bit [4] IRQ_FRAME_EN RW interrupt on any channel VALID [5] IRQ_ERR_EN RW interrupt on any channel CRC_ERR / OVERRUN / TEL_ABORT [7:6], reserved, read 0 0x28 RXTHRESH [11:0] RW high-time (cycles) above which a bit reads 1. Default (T0H + T1H) / 2 if written 0. 0x2C RXTIMEOUT [11:0] RW idle cycles that terminate/reset a partial frame. Default 2 × BITPERIOD if 0.

Cleared by writing 1 (see note on why not read-to-clear) [13] CRC_ERR RO/W1C frame received, CRC bad [14] OVERRUN RO/W1C a new frame completed before VALID was cleared [15] TEL_ABORT RO/W1C reply aborted by an incoming command edge 0x34 RXFRAME1 as above channel 1 0x38 RXFRAME2 as above channel 2 0x3C RXFRAME3 as above channel 3 0x40 TURNAROUND [15:0] RW cycles from command frame's last edge to reply start. DShot600 nominal 30 µs = 1500. 0x44 TELEMPERIOD [11:0] RW reply bit period in cycles. Default BITPERIOD × 4 / 5 if 0 (DShot600 → 67). 0x48 TELEM0 [11:0] {e[2:0], m[8:0]} RW eRPM period to reply on channel 0. Hardware appends CRC, GCR- encodes, transition-encodes. 0x4C TELEM1 RW channel 1 0x50 TELEM2 RW channel 2 0x54 TELEM3 RW channel 3 0x58 RXSTATUS [3:0] VALID[ch] · [7:4] CRC_ERR[ch] · [11:8] OVERRUN[ch] · [15:12] TEL_BUSY[ch] · [19:16] PAD_DIR[ch] (1 = driving) RO one-read snapshot of all four channels 0x5C RXIRQ [0] FRAME · [1] ERR RO/W1C interrupt pending flags Reset state: RX_EN=0 , all thresholds 0 (→ derived defaults), all pads input-disabled only if the wrapper's pad config leaves them so, see §7. Note on clearing VALID : W1C is the safe default and matches the other DG32 peripherals. Read-to-clear is not recommended: the lockstep checker mirrors bus reads to the CHECKER core two cycles late, so a read with a side-effect would be observed by both cores but the side-effect happens once, safe in practice, but it is exactly the kind of subtlety the design avoids elsewhere. Keep W1C.

6. Interrupts One new source into dgrid_irq (0xDF): dshot_rx_irq = (IRQ_FRAME_EN & |VALID) | (IRQ_ERR_EN & |(CRC_ERR|OVERRUN|TEL_ABORT)) . Level, cleared by W1C of the underlying flags. dgrid_irq has a 16-bit raw vector with bits 0–6 and 8 (attention, 2dom) used; bit 7 is 1'b0 today and is the natural slot ( rtl/dgrid_irq.sv:58 ). Bits 9–15 are also free. Follow the existing convention: add dshot_rx_i = 1'b0 as a defaulted port so the frozen lite netlist is unchanged when the port is left unconnected, and tie it explicitly in the top (sv2v drops port defaults). 7. Pad-ring change, the real cost of this feature The four DShot pads are io[26] P_PWM_AH , io[28] P_PWM_BH , io[30] P_PWM_CH , io[32] P_PWM_TRIG ( openframe/openframe_project_wrapper.v:134-136 ). Today they are class PC_OUT ( pad_class() at line 470: i >= P_PWM_AH && i <= P_PWM_TRIG ), i.e. gpio_dm = 110 , gpio_inp_dis = 1 , oeb tied to constant drive (lines 408–414). The wrapper already has the class we need: PC_BIDIR ( gpio_dm = 110 , gpio_inp_dis = 0 , oeb dynamic) is what QSPI IO0–3, I²C and the three GPIOs use. So the change is three edits, not a new pad mode: edit today required pad_class() io[26..32] → PC_OUT io[26], io[28], io[30], io[32] → PC_BIDIR ; io[27], io[29], io[31] stay PC_OUT oeb_v[P_PWM_AH/BH/CH/TRIG] gpio_loopback_zero (always drive) ~pad_oe[ch] from dgrid_dshot , through u_glue like gpio3_oeb (oeb is active-low) gpio_in[P_PWM_AH/BH/CH/TRIG] unused → dgrid_dshot.pad_i[3:0] through the top-level gpio_ib_mode_sel , gpio_vtrip_sel , gpio_slow_sel stay at their existing all-zero tie (CMOS input, standard trip), same as the other bidirectional pads.

Why it still carries risk: the whole per-pad config table rests on an item your tape-in notes flag, the exact gpio_dm / inp_dis encoding was never verified against the real OpenFrame template; TODO in the wrapper header, confirm before GATE-3. Four pads that switch direction at runtime make that verification mandatory. It is the same verification the QSPI and I²C pads need anyway, so this adds no new unknown, it raises the cost of an existing one. Bridge safety is preserved: the low-side pads io[27] AL , io[29] BL , io[31] CL are untouched and remain PC_OUT . When PINMUX[0]=0 (PWM role) pad_oe is forced high for all four muxed pads, so they behave exactly as today. Two more pad-level checks for the reviewer: 1. Idle level. PC_BIDIR ( dm=110 ) has no weak pull, the pull modes ( dm=010/011 ) are input-only classes in this wrapper, and gpio_dm is a static tie, not switchable at runtime. So when the pad is input and the FC is not driving, the line floats. Bidirectional DShot idles high, normal DShot idles low. Recommendation: require the external pull on the board (bidirectional-DShot ESC wiring already puts a pull-up on the FC side) and document it in the datasheet; do not attempt a runtime-switched gpio_dm . 2. Reset. busy_q resets to 0 ( rtl/dgrid_dshot.sv:74 ) and dshot_o to 0, so the TX engine does not drive

out of reset. pad_oe must follow: input during rst_n_i low, so a resetting DG32 never drives a line the FC is driving. Note this inverts the current reset behaviour of these four pads (today they drive 0 out of reset as PC_OUT ), the board must not rely on a hard low from AH/BH/CH during reset. AL/BL/CL are unchanged. 8. Timing, cost and verification Edge precision at 50 MHz (20 ns/cycle): the decision margin is T1H − T0H . DShot300: 63 cycles (±630 ns), trivial. DShot600: 31 cycles (±310 ns), comfortable. DShot1200: 15 cycles (±150 ns), works on paper, but the synchroniser's ±1-cycle sampling jitter plus FC- side jitter eats a third of it. Recommend DShot600 as the supported maximum; DShot1200 best-effort. Area estimate: per channel, 12-bit width counter, 16-bit RX shifter, 4-bit CRC, RX FSM (~70 flops); 21-bit reply shifter, 12-bit period counter, GCR/transition encoder (~50 flops); status/flags (~8). ×4 ≈ ~520 flops plus shared registers (~100) and 8 synchroniser flops. Roughly 1,500– 2,500 std cells, about 3–5% of the lite die's 50,550. Consistent with Ayaz's "cheap": the TX engine closes at 172.9 MHz against 50 MHz, and RX has no deeper logic. Verification plan (before integration, all standalone): 1. tb_dshot_rx, loopback: existing TX engine drives RX through a modelled pad at all four speeds; every throttle 0–2047 × telem 0/1; assert RXFRAME == transmitted and VALID . Also inject each single-bit corruption → assert CRC_ERR , never VALID . 2. Glitch/desync: inject a 40 ns glitch mid-frame; assert timeout resync and that the next frame decodes clean. 3. Overrun: two frames back-to-back without a read → OVERRUN .

4. tb_dshot_tel, reply stream captured by a reference FC decoder implementing G = s ^ (s>>1) + GCR table + CRC check, written independently from the encoder (not shared code). All 4096 period values. 5. Turnaround: assert pad_oe rises exactly TURNAROUND cycles after the last command edge and falls after bit 21; assert abort-on-incoming-edge releases OE within 1 cycle. 6. Bidirectional end-to-end: FC model sends inverted frame with inverted CRC; RX decodes; reply goes out inverted at 5/4 rate; FC model validates. 7. Integrated: re-run fwtest T- suite (T01–T17) bit-identical, plus a new T18 dshot_rx loopback on the FPGA using a jumper between two DShot pads. Lockstep: RX is a normal bus slave. Its registers are read by MAIN and mirrored to CHECKER like every other peripheral; no store timing depends on the asynchronous input, because decoding is in hardware. This is the property firmware bit-banging cannot provide. 9. SRAM: 28 KB vs 32 KB, separating the two questions Ayaz: "28 KB bare minimum, 32 KB with safety margin; the reusable buffer saves only 2 KB." That is a firmware footprint statement, and it is the right way to size memory. The 28 KB proposal was a floorplan lever: 16 → 14 macros lets 2dom's 17 macros fit 3 columns × 6 rows instead of 3 × 7, deleting an entire macro row and growing the full-width logic strip from 1.75 mm² to 3.40 mm², that is what makes 2dom fit the 2,900 µm wrapper slot at all. It was never a claim that firmware needs less memory.

Both can be true. The question is whether 2dom can fit at 2,900 µm with 32 KB, and the codex branch is already answering it empirically: 2dom/13 is a keep-32 KB spread-floorplan test, 2dom/12 a 24 KB variant. If 13 routes and closes, keep 32 KB and drop the 28 KB idea. If only the reduced-SRAM variants fit, then the firmware team gets 28 KB and the 2 KB reusable buffer stops being optional. Decide from those two runs, not from either side's estimate. Note the lite die is unaffected either way, it stays 32 KB. 10. What to implement, the list RTL 1. rtl/dgrid_dshot_rx.sv, per-channel RX decoder (§4.1), 4 instances, parameterised on TW=12 . 2. rtl/dgrid_dshot_tel.sv, per-channel GCR/transition reply engine (§4.2). 3. Extend dgrid_dshot.sv : registers 0x24–0x5C (§5), pad_i[3:0] input, pad_oe[3:0] output, irq_o , direction FSM (§4.3). Existing 0x00–0x20 behaviour and the TX engine unchanged; tb_dshot must still pass bit-identical. 4. dg32_lite_top.sv : route pad_i / pad_oe for the four muxed pads; OE forced high in PWM role; new IRQ source into dgrid_irq . Wrapper / pad ring 5. openframe_project_wrapper.v : io[26/28/30/32] PC_OUT → PC_BIDIR in pad_class() ; oeb_v for those four from ~pad_oe via u_glue ; gpio_in for those four to the top; OE deasserted in reset. Board-side pull documented (no on-die pull in this class). 6. Verify the OpenFrame per-pad control encoding against the real template, already a GATE-3 TODO; now blocking. Firmware / docs 7. dg32.h : register defines; fwtest T18 loopback test. 8. Datasheet: GPIO 14 → 3; DShot bidirectional "not supported" → "supported, DShot150–600, best-effort 1200"; document the pad-direction behaviour. 9. DG_lite_analysis.md item 9: reopen. Verification, §8 items 1–7.

Not in scope of this change: a new bus slot (kept at 0xC), timer input capture (not needed once RX is hardware), any change to the low-side PWM pads. 11. Open questions for Ayaz before implementation starts 1. Roles per pad, is DG32 ever both FC (TX) and ESC (RX) on different channels simultaneously? The spec allows it (per-channel direction), but if not required, a global role bit simplifies the FSM. 2. Reply on every frame ( TELEM_ALWAYS ) vs only on telem-request, which FC firmware are you targeting first? Betaflight bidirectional expects every frame. 3. Idle level: the bidirectional pad class has no on-die pull (§7). Is a board-side pull-up acceptable, or do you need the die to define the idle level? (The latter means a runtime- switched gpio_dm , which I recommend against.) 4. Reset behaviour change: AH/BH/CH/TRIG will float (input) during reset instead of driving 0 . Is anything on your board relying on the hard low? 5. Priority vs tape-in: this touches the wrapper's unverified pad config. It is not for the 16 Sep die. Confirm it targets the following shuttle (CI2612) alongside 2dom.

D E E P G R I D S E M I Chips made on older processes · Hyderabad, India PLAIN-LANGUAGE EDITION · v3 Angel / seed round · ₹10 Cr · September 2026 Mature-Node Silicon for India’s Defence and Industrial Base In plain words: the chips India buys from abroad, why we can make them here, and now, chip by chip, who buys each one, what it earns, and the rules that guard the money. India buys almost every one of its simpler chips from other countries. About $9 billion of them a year. These are the unexciting parts inside every vehicle, electricity meter, drone and defence box: power chips, small processors, motor drivers, data-line chips, voltage monitors. Nobody in India makes them. The reason is not skill. It is that designing a chip the normal way costs $2 to $5 million before you sell one unit, and these chips sell in small numbers. This document explains how we cut that cost by about ten times, what we have already built, what ₹10 Cr would buy, and, new in this edition, the money one chip at a time, the named anchor customers, and the stop rules we set for ourselves in advance.

DEEPGRID SEMI | Mature-Node Silicon for India’s Defence and Industrial Base PLAIN EDITION · CONFIDENTIAL PART ONE India buys almost every one of these chips from abroad Nobody in India makes them. The reason is money, not skill. And money can be changed. 1 What India buys, and why nobody here makes it Start with one number. Last year India imported $23.4 billion of chips. That figure is from UN COMTRADE, code HS 8542. It is the only number in this section that comes from outside our company. About 70 % of it came from China and Taiwan. Inside that total, analysts estimate about $9 billion a year is the kind of chip this document is about. These are chips made on older, larger factory processes, 130 nanometres and above. Power management chips. Small microcontrollers. Motor gate drivers. Data-line transceivers. Voltage supervisors. Electricity- meter front ends. These are not exciting chips. But they are most of the chips in any product. A car has one or two advanced processors and several dozen of these older ones. A smart electricity meter has none of the advanced kind at all. So the import bill is large, and it stays large. DeepGrid Semi Pvt Ltd · CIN U62099TS2024PTC183631 · T-Hub Phase 2, Hyderabad 6
